MATERIALS / THE WOOD

A grain worth
getting to know.

The collection concept uses solid hardwood rather than veneer over particleboard. Natural colour and grain variation are part of the material, not a flaw.

Wood responds to humidity. Give it a stable indoor climate and space to move. Request current sourcing and finish documentation from a real maker.

WOOL

MATERIALS / THE FABRIC

Comfort with
a little texture.

Belgian linen, wool flannel and bouclé define the supplied collection. Touch, weave and tone matter as much as the silhouette.

Removable covers and replacement cover availability are part of the concept specification. A real purchase needs current fabric care, composition and testing information.

See it in person ↗
MATERIALS / THE JOINERY

Nothing to hide.

Mortise and tenon, dovetails and dowels. The idea is to let the way a piece is built be visible, rather than concealed.

The concept specifies a 10-year structural warranty. This demonstration issues no warranty or certification; inspect a real manufacturer's terms before purchase.

03 / CARE & COVER

Built for the long view.

The brief proposes 10-year structural and 3-year finish/fabric cover. Confirm actual terms with a real retailer.

Read our care guide

Dust wood with a soft cloth, use coasters and dry spills promptly. Keep furniture away from direct heat and strong sunlight. Vacuum upholstery gently and follow the specific fabric cleaning code. Avoid soaking natural fibres; seek professional cleaning guidance when needed.
